faq_1_answer: Returned Goods Relief (RGR) is a UK customs provision that can remove import duty and VAT when goods previously exported from the UK return to the country, subject to conditions. It is designed to avoid paying import duties twice on the same goods.
faq_2_question: What are the eligibility criteria for RGR?
faq_2_answer: The goods must have been exported or transported from the UK in free circulation, must be the same goods being returned, must come back within three years and must not have been altered abroad. Proper evidence of the original export and the return is required.
faq_3_question: How long do I have to re-import goods to claim RGR?
faq_3_answer: Goods must be re-imported within three years of the date of export.
faq_4_question: Can I claim VAT relief as well as customs duty relief?
faq_4_answer: Possibly, but VAT relief has its own conditions. The person re-importing the goods generally has to be the person who exported them, and any VAT that was zero-rated on export has to be paid on return. If the importer is not the exporter, or does not own the returning goods, import VAT is normally due.
faq_5_question: Does Returned Goods Relief cover excise duty?
faq_5_answer: No. Relief from excise duty is not available under Returned Goods Relief.

faq_6_question: What documentation and evidence is needed to claim RGR?
faq_6_answer: Evidence usually includes the original export declaration, import records, invoices, transport documents, product identifiers and records showing that the goods have not been materially changed. You need to be able to show that the goods met the conditions at the time of export, and HMRC may ask for additional supporting documents.
faq_7_question: What if I already paid duty on returned goods?
faq_7_answer: The opportunity may not be lost. Keep your export, import and product documentation and contact TDR. We will review the situation and contact Customs on your behalf. Time limits apply to repayment claims: HMRC allows three years for overpayments, for example.
faq_8_question: Can customer returns from the EU or other countries qualify?
faq_8_answer: Yes, customer returns of goods that were exported from the UK may qualify when they are re-imported, if the conditions above are met. For eCommerce, each return needs to be matched to the original export and to the person who exported it. Items that have been worn or tried on are not eligible.
faq_9_question: Is Returned Goods Relief the same as duty drawback?
faq_9_answer: No. Returned Goods Relief removes duty and VAT at the moment qualifying goods are re-imported. Duty drawback is a refund of duty that was previously paid. Which one applies depends on how the goods moved and how duty was handled. See our UK duty drawback page for the refund route.
faq_10_answer: TDR can review your shipment data and operating process to identify potentially eligible movements and the evidence needed to support future declarations and recovery opportunities. Thanks to our access to HMRC data, we pull down the information we need so that we only require from you the documentation to substantiate the claim.
conditions-title: When does Returned Goods Relief apply in the UK?
conditions-intro: Returned Goods Relief (RGR) lets you re-import goods that were previously exported from the UK without paying import duty and VAT a second time, as long as the conditions below are met. For online retailers, the most common case is a customer return that crosses the border back into the UK.
conditions-item1: The goods were exported or transported from the UK in free circulation.
conditions-item2: They are re-imported within three years of export.
conditions-item3: They come back as the same goods, without being altered abroad.
conditions-item4: For VAT relief, the person re-importing the goods is the person who exported them, and any VAT zero-rated on export is paid on return.
conditions-item5: Excise duty is not covered by Returned Goods Relief.
conditions-callout-title: Why “duty and VAT free” is not automatic
conditions-callout-description: Relief has to be claimed on the import declaration and supported by evidence. If it is missed or the evidence is incomplete, duty and VAT can be charged on goods that should have come back relief-free.
ecom-title: Returned Goods Relief for eCommerce returns
ecom-intro: Every customer return is a separate re-import. For retailers shipping from the UK to EU or other overseas customers, that means a high volume of small movements, each of which needs to be linked to its original export.
ecom-list-title: Where eCommerce claims usually go wrong
ecom-item1: The original export cannot be matched to the returning parcel.
ecom-item2: The returns provider or 3PL imports the goods under a different entity from the one that exported them, which affects VAT relief.
ecom-item3: Export proof sits in different systems and is hard to retrieve for each return.
ecom-item4: The goods are not in the state in which they left: worn or tried-on items are not eligible.
ecom-item5: The relief is not applied at import, and nobody revisits the return afterwards.
ecom-description: TDR connects the outbound shipment to the return, identifies which returns qualify and prepares the evidence. If duty has already been paid, we review whether it can be recovered.
